findings.claim: The learning window and observed score clocks span [0.0, 0.49] with 50 observed score nodes; curve support is [0.0, 0.49], so no extrapolation beyond the observed window is licensed.
The objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; coordinate contrasts are therefore not themselves the affinity objective.

For landmark_00_local_dx the observed curve is non-monotone: it rises to a mid-window maximum near t~0.11, falls to a minimum near t~0.19, partially recovers, and ends near its starting level (whole-window z ~ -0.18). The trend table reports 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts, and the quadratic fit is not accepted (relative node RMSE ~0.78), so a single global linear or quadratic direction is not supported.

The first-node and last-node rates for landmark_00_local_dx have opposite signs (first_rate_z ~ -17.5, last_rate_z ~ +8.1) with 14 independent batches, indicating a changing local direction rather than a stationary target across the window.

hypotheses.direction: non-monotone: positive early, negative mid-window, weakly positive late
hypotheses.falsifier: A re-read of the same curve on independent batches showing a monotone trend with no sign change, or an accepted low-RMSE polynomial fit with a single consistent sign of rate.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_local_dx curve over the observed score nodes
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed window [0.0, 0.49]; all seeds
hypotheses.statement: Landmark_00_local_dx shows a reproducible early-window rise followed by a mid-window reversal and late-window partial recovery, so a stage-dependent (time-varying) coordinate contrast is a better description than a single fixed endpoint target for this coordinate.

hypotheses.direction: stage-dependent relevance rather than a fixed coordinate direction
hypotheses.falsifier: Evidence that the early and late contrasts share the same sign and magnitude within batch noise, which would make a constant schedule sufficient.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_local_dx curve and its first/last rate signs
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed window; all seeds
hypotheses.statement: Because the landmark_00_local_dx contrast changes sign within the window, a constant-blend or single-direction reward on this coordinate would average incompatible early and late contrasts; a staged relevance schedule is the appropriate candidate to test at fixed dose.

limitations: Only one coordinate feature (landmark_00_local_dx) was read as an actual curve; the remaining 199 curve features were not inspected, so no claim is made about them.
Stage profiles and temporal profiles are unavailable; no data-derived knot or stage boundary is supported, and the registered knots remain experimental hypotheses rather than discovered stages.

The observed curve is a coordinate contrast in predicted endpoint world coordinates; it does not by itself specify an absolute coordinate target, spatial gradient, or any energy/chemical interpretation.
Selection preference and survival are not measured here; no descendant-survival or final-affinity-improvement claim is made from these coordinate curves.
Current study quality results are withheld; no performance or improvement claim is made.
